name: The complainers at Taberah and the lusters at Kibroth-hattaavah
charge: Complaining against the Lord after the deliverance, and lusting after the food of Egypt behind the mixed multitude
summary: The Most High hates it when his people complain. He had just destroyed Egypt for them, and at the first trial on the far side of the sea they complained, and the fire of the Lord burnt in the outskirts of the camp. Then the mixed multitude fell a lusting, and Israel followed them and wept for the fish and the cucumbers and the garlick of the house of bondage, despising angels’ food that agreed to every taste. Quail came, and with the quail a plague, and the graves of lust are the name of the place.
offenseFull: When the people complained it displeased the Lord, and he heard it, and his anger was kindled (Numbers 11:1). He had just destroyed Egypt for Israel, its land, its firstborn and its army in the sea, and at the first trial on the other side they jumped off his bandwagon. Nothing spoken behind closed doors is hidden. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, the ear of jealousy hears all things, and a murmuring that is unprofitable is to be refrained from, for no word so secret shall go for nothing, and the mouth that lies slays the soul (Wisdom of Solomon 1:8-11). A problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High himself.
Then the mixed multitude that was among them fell a lusting, and the children of Israel

also wept again (Numbers 11:4). The mixed multitude were the other nations sprinkled in among Israel that went up with them out of Egypt, and the law appointed what they were to be, bondmen and bondmaids, not Israel’s example (Exodus 12:38; Leviticus 25:44-45). It was not Israel complaining first. The nations lusted after the food of Egypt, and the children of Israel, gullible and assimilated as always, followed right after them, remembering the fish they ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlick (Numbers 11:5). They wept for the diet of the house of bondage weeks after the bondage ended, and they had just watched the fire consume the complainers in the outermost parts of the camp and went back and did the same thing. And what they despised was angels’ food, sent from heaven without their labour, which they had only to pick up, able to content every man’s delight and agreeing to every taste, tempering itself to every man’s liking, so that whatever the tongue craved that day the manna tasted like it (Psalms 78:25; Wisdom of Solomon 16:20-21). They tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust (Psalms 78:18). The same spirit is on the people in this captivity, comfortable with the entertainments and the table of the oppressor.
judgmentFull: At Taberah the fire of the Lord burnt among them and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp; the people cried to Moses, and when Moses prayed to the Lord the fire was quenched, and the place was named for the burning (Numbers 11:1-3). The weight of carrying them fell on Moses, who asked the Lord why he had afflicted his servant and laid the burden of all this people upon him, and whether he had conceived them all, that he should carry them in his bosom as a nursing father, and said that if this was how it was to be, let him be killed out of hand (Numbers 11:11-15). He was carrying grown people who behaved like children.

The reason for the second judgment was stated plainly: because they had despised the Lord which is among them and had wept before him, asking why they came out of Egypt, they would eat flesh not one day nor two nor five nor ten nor twenty, but a whole month, until it came out at their nostrils and was loathsome to them (Numbers 11:18-20). When Moses asked how it could be done for six hundred thousand footmen, the Lord answered by asking whether the Lord’s hand had waxed short (Numbers 11:23). A wind from the Lord brought quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, two cubits high upon the face of the earth, and while the flesh was yet between their teeth, before it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled and he smote the people with a very great plague; and the place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, the graves of lust, because there they buried the people that lusted (Numbers 11:31-34). He gave them their request, but sent leanness into their soul (Psalms 106:15). The lesson also stands in nature: excess of meat brings sickness, and many have perished by surfeiting, but he that takes heed prolongs his life (Ecclesiasticus 37:29-31). These things were our examples, to the intent that we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted (1 Corinthians 10:6).

lawsResolved.text: Gluttony and excessiveness is iniquity and leads to a carnal outlook on life.
We are not to have a primary desire for earthly things.

text.text: And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.
Therefore he that speaketh unrighteous things cannot be hid: neither shall vengeance, when it punisheth, pass by him.
For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words shall come unto the Lord for the manifestation of his wicked deeds.
For the ear of jealousy heareth all things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.
Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.
And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.
Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.
Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.
We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
Man did eat angels’ food: he sent them meat to the full.
Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels’ food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.
For thy sustenance declared thy sweetness unto thy children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.
And they tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust.

And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord: and the Lord heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.
And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched.
And he called the name of the place Taberah: because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.
And Moses said unto the Lord, Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?

Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?
Whence should I have flesh to give unto all this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.
I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.

And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh: for ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore the Lord will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days;

But even a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you: because that ye have despised the Lord which is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?
And the Lord said unto Moses, Is the Lord’s hand waxed short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.

And there went forth a wind from the Lord, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day’s journey on this side, and as it were a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.

And the people stood up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered ten homers: and they spread them all abroad for themselves round about the camp.
And while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the Lord was kindled against the people, and the Lord smote the people with a very great plague.
And he called the name of that place Kibroth–hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.
And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul.
Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats:
For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.
By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.
Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.
And the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna, before our eyes.
Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.

And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh: for ye have wept in the ears of the Lord, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore the Lord will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days;

But even a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you: because that ye have despised the Lord which is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?
And Moses said, The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month.
Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?
And the Lord said unto Moses, Is the Lord’s hand waxed short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.
